candidates.title: Impact of super resolution deep learning reconstruction with a 1024 matrix on CAD-RADS classification of intermediate coronary stenosis: A bicentric retrospective study
candidates.abstract: Introduction Moderate coronary stenosis (CAD-RADS 3) is a diagnostic gray zone in coronary CT angiography (CCTA). We evaluated whether super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR), particularly with a 1024 matrix, modifies CAD-RADS classification and inter-reader agreement. Materials and methods: Thirty-nine CCTA examinations from two centers, each containing at least one 50–69% stenosis identified on the routine normal-resolution deep learning reconstruction (NR-DLR), were reconstructed with NR-DLR and SR-DLR (512 and 1024 matrices). Five experienced readers blindly assigned CAD-RADS categories. Agreement was assessed with Gwet's AC2 and paired reclassification with exact McNemar tests. Subgroup analyses (plaque composition, initial image quality) were exploratory. Results Forty-six lesions were analyzed (19 calcified, 16 mixed, 10 non-calcified, one in-stent). Agreement remained excellent (AC2 0.89 [0.86–0.92], 0.87 [0.83–0.90] and 0.84 [0.81–0.88] for NR-DLR, SR-DLR-512 and SR-DLR-1024). Consensus CAD-RADS 2 rose from 6.5% to 21.7% with SR-DLR-1024 (p = 0.016; 10 lesions downgraded, 2 upgraded), predominantly in lesions with non-calcified components. Per-reader CAD-RADS 2 rates ranged from 13% to 30%, increasing significantly for two of five readers (p = 0.004). Conclusion SR-DLR-1024 modified CAD-RADS classification in about one fifth of intermediate lesions while preserving excellent agreement. Without an invasive reference standard, these reclassifications reflect a change in reader interpretation rather than a proven gain in accuracy.

candidates.title: Explainable Multimodal AI Approach to Reduce Unnecessary Breast Biopsies
candidates.abstract: Recently, there has been rise in multimodal vision-language models for computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), yet their application in breast diagnosis, particularly for predicting biopsy outcomes remains limited. This study presents a multimodal vision-language approach, incorporating Grad-CAM as an Explainable AI (XAI) technique, to predict benign tumors in patients recommended for biopsy, especially those classified as BI-RADS 4 and 5. A novel multimodal framework was devel- oped using Vision Transformer (ViT) for imaging feature extraction and DeBERTa-V3-Large for textual embeddings. The model was trained and evaluated on a comprehensive in-house dataset comprising 1,632 patients, each with four mammography views and a corresponding radiology report. The features of both modalities were extracted independently and fused by late fusion before classification. Grad-CAM was used to generate visual explanations highlighting key regions influencing model predictions. The proposed model demonstrated high sensitivity 90%, 95%, 99%, and 100% with corresponding specificities of 40%, 36%, 18%, and 11%, respectively. The best AUC achieved was 0.72 by multimodal approach on the test set, outperforming the image only (0.66) and text-only (0.68) baselines. The proposed multimodal architecture, enhanced with Grad-CAM, demonstrates a strong potential to identify benign tumors among high-risk patients, offering interpretable insights and thereby helping reduce unnecessary biopsies, patient anxiety, and healthcare costs.

candidates.title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
candidates.abstract: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits. Proactive defenses aim to prevent such manipulations by adding an imperceptible perturbation before an image is shared. Existing defenses for DiT-based in-context editors make the output attend less to the protected reference image. But this leaves the model free to follow the edit instruction using the text and its own generated tokens, often producing a new, weakly grounded image rather than preventing the edit. We find that the opposite strategy is more effective: instead of leading the model to ignore the reference, we encourage it to copy it. Through controlled attention interventions, we show that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior, causing the model to reproduce its input, often as a lossy copy, rather than execute the requested transformation. Based on this insight, we introduce Copying-as-Defense (CaD), which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks. Since attention rows are normalized, increasing reference attention suppresses the attention allocated to the text and generated canvas. Restricting the objective to early blocks also lets us truncate the backpropagation path, keeping optimization cheap. Across editors and benchmarks, CaD reduces average edit success from 81.4% on unprotected images to 24.0%, a 70.6% relative reduction, and by a further 44.3% relative to DeContext, the strongest baseline (43.0%). CaD is also roughly 1.8-2.0x faster per optimization step than comparable methods.

candidates.title: Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling: A Material-Removal-Centric Framework for Three-Dimensional Shape Generation
candidates.abstract: Three-dimensional shape generation has been studied through a variety of representations and learning paradigms, including voxel-based generation, point-cloud synthesis, implicit neural representations, neural radiance fields, Gaussian-based scene representations, and procedural computer-aided design (CAD) generation. Despite their differences, many approaches primarily formulate generation as the direct synthesis or reconstruction of a target representation. This paper proposes Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling (STGM), a material-removal-centric framework that formulates three-dimensional shape generation as the progressive transformation of an initial stock into a target solid through a sequence of removal operations. Instead of generating the final geometry exclusively as a static representation, STGM models the evolving residual material state, the geometry of each removal region, the ordering of operations, and the compatibility of each operation with manufacturing constraints. The framework combines a geometric state representation, a conditional removal policy, differentiable or approximately differentiable geometric updates, and a multi-objective optimization procedure. Its objectives include target-shape fidelity, preservation of required material, operation complexity, accessibility, and estimated manufacturing cost. A hierarchical strategy is proposed to organize coarse removal, intermediate structural formation, and fine geometric refinement. The paper defines a formal problem, presents a reference algorithm, specifies a training objective, and develops an experimental protocol for evaluating geometric accuracy, trajectory quality, manufacturability, and computational efficiency. STGM is presented as a research hypothesis rather than an empirically validated method. Its potential contribution lies in integrating material-state evolution and removal-sequence optimization into a unified generative formulation, while its novelty and effectiveness require systematic comparison with existing CAD sequence generation, constructive solid geometry, machining-aware modeling, and shape-generation approaches.

candidates.title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

candidates.title: EDA-Agent: A Multi-Agent AI System for RTL Verification, Circuit Debugging, and Semiconductor Design Automation -TCAD-2026-2322 (IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems)
candidates.abstract: Hardware verification and debugging traditionally consume over 70% of digital Integrated Circuit (IC) design cycles. Engineers spend thousands of hours manually parsing static timing reports, inspecting Value Change Dump (VCD) waveform traces, and writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA). EDA-Agent is an open-source, multi-agent AI platform designed to automate Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code analysis, functional testbench generation, waveform failure debugging, synthesis area estimation, and timing slack optimization. To overcome the hallucination risks of pure neural generation, EDA-Agent employs a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with strict deterministic boundaries: AST Static Analysis: A custom regex/AST parser deterministically evaluates design violations, such as latch inference conditions and blocking assignment race hazards. Trace-Based VCD Waveform Debugging: The system parses standard IEEE 1364 VCD files to build a temporal transition matrix, allowing the agent to back-track state transitions and map assertion failures directly to faulty source code lines. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): The system grounds its reasoning in an indexed database of IEEE 1800-2017 SystemVerilog standards, Yosys manuals, and OpenSTA documentation. Empirical evaluations of EDA-Agent demonstrate 100% unit test accuracy on core parsing components, 94.2% waveform-based bug localization accuracy, and a 37.5x acceleration in SystemVerilog testbench generation compared to manual human workflows.

candidates.title: Dual-graph computable knowledge engineering for CAD-to-CNC macro synthesis
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize G-code, but autonomous CAD-to-CNC macro-generation must preserve geometry, process constraints, variable roles, equations, loop bounds, coordinate mappings, and controller syntax. This paper presents a dual-graph computable knowledge engineering method in which typed knowledge objects are selected by a semantic relation graph and converted by a computational dependency graph into acyclic variable-expression-loop dependencies. A seven-layer Macro-Structured Parametric CNC Code (Macro-SPCC) schema and Macro-Program Intermediate Representation (MPIR) organize the evidence, while deterministic modules perform evaluation, geometric checking, and FANUC Macro B compilation. Across 12 tire-mold lettering-insert tasks from six DXF cases and two toolpath configurations, the method achieved 91.7% accuracy, 50.0 percentage points above Text-RAG, and a 100.0% compilation pass rate. VERICUT confirmed continuity, endpoint reachability, and safe retraction, demonstrating a traceable, computationally closed, and executable synthesis process.

candidates.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD, a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that renders node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.

candidates.title: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design of Electronic Devices and Circuits
candidates.abstract: Abstract Driven by the miniaturization of single components, which has reached few nanometers, chips can nowadays accommodate hundreds of billions of transistors. As a result, modern nanoelectronics devices and systems are becoming extremely complex. To remain truly effective, computer-aided design (CAD) tools must evolve in parallel with these advancements, keeping pace with the increasing demands of scale and functionality. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has seen an incredible development in several areas. In nanoelectronics, ML is already offering promising technological solutions that improve performance and provide predictions across the entire electronic design stack. From material properties to quantum transport and circuit behavior, ML techniques are making simulation workflows much more efficient and flexible, leading to a new paradigm of CAD: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design. This review examines the latest developments in computer simulations for assessing the performance of electronic systems and the types of models used across the different levels of abstraction. We also discuss the challenges that still need to be addressed, especially the need for physics-based ML models, and explore future directions toward generative machine learning frameworks tailored specifically for electronic system design.

candidates.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
candidates.abstract: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.

candidates.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
candidates.abstract: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), recent studies have shown that final answers do not always depend on the generated rationales. In particular, LLMs may rely on query-specific shortcuts rather than the information provided by their reasoning steps. In this paper, we investigate whether context-aware decoding (CAD), an existing contrastive decoding method, can mitigate such shortcut behavior when applied to CoT reasoning. We study this application as Rationale Contrastive Decoding (RCD), which contrasts the next-token distributions conditioned on the query with and without its rationale, amplifying tokens whose likelihood increases due to the rationale. We provide a theoretical interpretation of this decoding rule via a KL-regularized reward-maximization objective. Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RCD improves answer accuracy over standard CoT. Furthermore, intervention analyses using ground-truth and random rationales reveal that RCD increases the behavioral dependence of final answers on the rationale content. Our findings suggest that contrastive decoding offers a simple, training-free approach to mitigating query shortcuts.

candidates.title: Deterministic Spatial Synthesis: A Compiler Architecture for LLM-Driven CAD-to-Blueprint Translation in Synthetic Environment Infrastructure (SEI)
candidates.abstract: Generative Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently exhibit non-deterministic variances when generating spatial geometries, rendering them susceptible to structural hallucination in production CAD pipelines. This paper introduces Synthetic Environment Infrastructure (SEI)—a deterministic compiler architecture converting natural language parametric constraints into validated blueprints via Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), Domus Mare FEA hydro-envelopes (180 kN·m capacity), and Think Furniture joinery compilation.

candidates.title: Leonardo's CAD - La Geometria Svelata / Dal modulo alla prospettiva: la griglia generativa di Leonardo e il Braccio Fiorentino nell'Adorazione dei Magi. Una rilettura tecnica del disegno degli Uffizi (inv. 436 E). (it) Leonardo's CAD - The Revealed Geometry / From modulus to perspective: Leonardo's generative grid and the Florentine Braccio in the Adoration of the Magi. A technical reinterpretation of the Uffizi Drawing (inv. 436 E). (en) App di supporto alla ricerca accademica (it) / Academic Research Support App (en)
candidates.abstract: Premessa Leonardo’s CAD non è una ricerca isolata. È un pannello del trittico Leonardo’s Spatial Grammar, insieme a Leonardo’s Rulers e a Leonardo’s Score: tre indagini nate separate, una sola grammatica metrico-modulare dello spazio. Quella utilizzata da Leonardo da Vinci per costruire i suoi spazi prospettici. Il corpus, depositato su Zenodo, contesta l’idea di una prospettiva albertiana a scacchiera applicata in modo uniforme. Dall’Annunciazione all’Adorazione fino al Cenacolo, Leonardo lascia nel quadro i moduli con cui ha misurato: bugne e mattonelle (geometria inserita), la maglia 4:3 (geometria svelata), i ritmi degli arazzi e dei cassettoni (geometria intonata). Metodo La ricerca adotta un approccio di retroingegneria: parte da ciò che è visibile e misurabile nelle opere per ricostruire i principi metrici e modulari che ne organizzano lo spazio. Funzione dell’app L’app è uno strumento di supporto alla ricerca accademica: non la sostituisce, ma la integra, rendendone più accessibili e immediatamente comprensibili i risultati più significativi. È tuttora in fase di sviluppo e viene progressivamente aggiornata con l’avanzamento degli studi. Preface Leonardo’s CAD is not an isolated inquiry. It is one panel of the triptych Leonardo’s Spatial Grammar, with Leonardo’s Rulers and Leonardo’s Score: three inquiries born apart, one metric-modular grammar of space. The grammar Leonardo da Vinci used to construct his perspectival spaces. The corpus, deposited on Zenodo, challenges the idea of an Albertian checkerboard perspective applied uniformly. From the Annunciation through the Adoration to the Last Supper, Leonardo leaves in the picture the modules he measured with: ashlars and tiles (inserted geometry), the 4:3 mesh (revealed geometry), the rhythms of the tapestries and coffers (tuned geometry). The method is reverse engineering, starting from what can be seen and measured. This app was developed to highlight the most significant findings of the research. Method The research adopts a reverse-engineering approach: it begins with what is visible and measurable in the works to reconstruct the metric and modular principles that organize their space. Purpose of the App The app is designed to support academic research: it does not replace it but complements it by making its most significant findings more accessible and easier to understand. It is still under development and is progressively updated as the research advances. Giancarlo De Leo 20 ottobre 2026

candidates.title: Generative AI for Mechanical Systems Design: A Systematic Review of Language-Driven, Diffusion-Based, and Physics-Informed Approaches — Protocol for a Two-Tier Systematic Map and In-Depth Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Protocol of a systematic review on generative artificial intelligence for the design of mechanical systems, components and structures (2021–2026). The review covers three paradigms: language-driven approaches (large language models, vision-language models, LLM agents, CAD-as-language models), diffusion-based approaches (denoising diffusion, latent diffusion, flow matching) and physics-informed generative approaches. It uses a two-tier design: (1) a systematic map of all eligible studies, coded by paradigm, design task, design stage, design representation and evaluation type; (2) an in-depth critical synthesis of a core set of studies that quantitatively evaluate the physical validity, constraint satisfaction or manufacturability of generated designs, selected with criteria fixed before full-text assessment. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Searches were run in Scopus and Web of Science on 20 October 2026; this registration was made after title/abstract screening and before full-text assessment and data extraction.

candidates.title: Prediction of Deep Neural Network for TCAD Analysis of Degradation Induced by Near-Interface Displacement Defects in 4H-SiC MOSFETs
candidates.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices used in space and nuclear environments are exposed to radiation that creates displacement defects, and the effect of these defects near the gate oxide/SiC interface has not been analyzed systematically. This paper analyzes the effects of displacement defects (DDs) near this interface in a 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) on the threshold voltage (Vth), transconductance (gm), and on-current (Ion) using technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, and builds deep neural network (DNN) models that predict these effects. The DDs were modeled as acceptor-like traps, and their energy level, concentration, depth, lateral position, and distribution width were varied. The degradation was largest when the traps were located in the channel and at the edge of the junction field-effect transistor (JFET) region, and the depth mattered little as long as the trap region reached the interface. In addition, shallow-level traps reduced Ion without shifting Vth, whereas deep-level traps also increased Vth. All three DNN models for Vth, gm, and Ion reproduced the TCAD simulation results with high accuracy. Because the trained DNNs can rapidly predict the degradation for trap conditions not used in training within the valid range, they can be used for radiation reliability assessment of SiC MOSFETs.

candidates.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
candidates.abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

candidates.title: COMPUTER AND ENGINEERING GRAPHICS IN TRANSITION THROUGH A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DISTANCE EDUCATION RESEARCH
candidates.abstract: Distance learning is increasingly relevant in technical education, particularly in engineering and computer graphics. The integration of digital technologies enables the development of students’ spatial visualization and creative design skills essential for modern engineering practice. This review examines how distance education has transformed teaching and learning in these fields by analyzing global studies from 2014 to 2025. Although online delivery presents challenges in visualization and interactivity, advances such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation-based environments, and virtual laboratories are helping to bridge these gaps. The review identifies diverse program types, ranging from foundational design graphics to advanced applications in artificial intelligence, data science, and augmented reality. Despite significant progress, limited empirical evidence exists on learning outcomes and engagement. Through bibliometric analysis, this study maps thematic trends and collaboration patterns, offering evidence-based insights to enhance the quality and accessibility of engineering graphics education in the digital era

candidates.title: OV-PEAR: Observation-Verified Pose-Scale Estimation and Reconstruction for Unknown Industrial Manipulation Objects
candidates.abstract: Fine industrial robotic manipulation requires 6D pose, scale, and an operation-ready 3D model. Existing industrial pose estimation relies on CAD models, object-specific training data, or stable workcells, limiting use with unseen objects; zero-shot methods suffer from single-view occlusion, generative bias, and scale uncertainty. We present OV-PEAR, an observation-verified framework for 3D reconstruction and pose-scale estimation of unknown industrial objects. Its three-stage object-centric pipeline: (1) segments RGB-D instances and generates object-level 3D hypotheses; (2) anchors them to the robot frame via appearance-aware view retrieval, explicit scale search, and visibility-sensitive registration; (3) back-projects multi-view RGB-D evidence into the object-canonical frame to verify voxel occupancy, suppress hallucinations, and produce reusable trusted object models. On BOP-Industrial, OV-PEAR achieves 0.657 average AR and improves pose and voxel-level geometric consistency in real scenes; real-robot connector assembly reaches 99.67% grasp and 84.00% assembly success. The model library and pose-scale log enable short-term object-level state maintenance at 0.02 ms/frame.

candidates.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering-Grade Parametric CAD: A Critical Review of Representations, Large Language Models, and Agentic Design Systems
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding computer-aided design (CAD) from shape generation toward generative, conversational, and agentic engineering. However, most AI–CAD evaluations remain dominated by geometric similarity and execution success, while industrial CAD depends on editable parameters, design intent, stable feature histories, manufacturing constraints, and downstream CAD/CAE reuse. This structured critical review synthesizes 107 sources, principally from 2020–2026, across constrained sketches, boundary representations (B-Reps), parametric sequences, executable CAD programs, large language and multimodal models, CAD agents, commercial-CAD integration, and CAD–CAE. Rather than organizing the field only by model family, the review compares methods through the engineering information preserved and the behavior of generated models after modification. The synthesis identifies a consistent evidence gap: geometric validity and program execution are increasingly strong, whereas native feature-tree robustness, persistent references, design-intent preservation, and downstream verification remain weakly benchmarked. To address this gap, we propose the engineering-grade AI–CAD (EG–CAD) framework, in which geometric validity and executability are mandatory gates followed by parametric editability, constraint/design-intent preservation, feature-history robustness, engineering compliance, and downstream usability. A reference agent architecture and staged roadmap connect these criteria to CAD/CAM/CAE and smart-manufacturing workflows, reframing AI–CAD as an engineering automation problem rather than a shape-generation task.

candidates.title: Foundation models in reverse engineering, CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing: A systematic review
candidates.abstract: Reverse engineering is undergoing a profound transformation driven by the emergence of foundation models. These models, together with their applications, are progressively extending the limits of artificial intelligence (AI) from geometrical reconstruction to a more sophisticated level engineering reasoning. In contrast to traditional methods, which usually use sequences of algorithms for specific 3D retrieval and reconstruction tasks, current foundation models train geometrical representations that are able to support semantic reasoning, computer-aided design (CAD) reconstruction, and intelligent manufacturing in a unified way. This work provides an overview of foundation models within the context of reverse engineering and their combination with CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing. Starting from a systematic bibliometric analysis of the recent literature, the present review is mainly focused on the development of representation learning and reviews the key geometric forms that are being used by the current foundation models. The paper also explores the engineering abilities facilitated by such models in the reverse engineering process. Furthermore, current challenges, research obstacles, and future directions are critically explored, emphasizing the recent transition toward intelligent engineering systems. The analysis shows that foundation models are gradually making reverse engineering move from being an assortment of discrete computational activities to becoming an engineering process workflow that is made possible by means of geometry representations and multimodal reasoning as well as engineering AI. Finally, considerations on the importance of developing engineering conceptual frameworks to interpret the emerging role of foundation models in future intelligent engineering systems are drafted.

candidates.title: Exploring an Agent-Based Generative AI CAD Framework Enhancing CAD Design Automation with AI-Driven Parametric Modelling and Adaptive Query Generation
An algorithm for 6D object pose estimation based on generative single-image 3D reconstruction
candidates.abstract: Reliable 6D object pose estimation is a foundational capability for robotic manipulation in Industry 4.0 and unstructured warehouse environments. Current state-of-the-art methods, such as PVN3D and SAM-6D, predominantly rely on “Model-Based” paradigms that necessitate high-fidelity CAD models of the target objects for training or template matching. This requirement severely limits their applicability in open-world scenarios where such CAD models are unavailable in real-time. To bridge this gap, a novel 6D Pose Estimation Framework without fine-tuning on the target object (Zero-Shot) is proposed to eliminate the dependency on prior CAD models. A single-view 3D generative model is leveraged to synthesize a geometrically plausible 3D mesh from a single RGB image. To address the scale ambiguity inherent in generative models, which poses a critical challenge for robotic grasping, a Template-Prior Iterative Closest Point (TP-ICP) based on the classical ICP is introduced for iterative recovery of the metric scale. This algorithm robustly recovers the metric physical scale of the neural-generated mesh using depth information, employing median-based outlier removal and template-guided ICP to handle occlusions and sensor noise. The recovered metric mesh is then seamlessly integrated into a standard 6D pose estimation pipeline, establishing a closed-loop framework comprising model self-generation, metric scale calibration, and pose estimation. A fully reproducible implementation scheme is presented. Systematic experiments on the LINEMOD dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves robust 6D pose estimation suitable for robotic tasks, even in the complete absence of prior CAD models.

candidates.title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
candidates.abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

candidates.title: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling
candidates.abstract: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling is an open-access, accreditation-aligned curriculum module developed under the PREP4UNI.ONLINE OER Initiative for undergraduate engineering candidates, mechanical designers, and STEM educators. Structured in accordance with the Washington Accord, EUR-ACE, and IEA Global Engineering Competency frameworks, this module bridges fundamental mechanics of materials with modern 3D CAD modeling, finite element simulation, and design for manufacturing. Key Analytical & Technical Coverage: Continuum Failure Theories: Von Mises distortion energy multi-axial yield criteria, Modified Goodman and ASME elliptic dynamic fatigue limits, and preloaded bolted joint compliance. Machine Element Synthesis: Circular power transmission shafting under combined torsion and bending, Marin endurance limit factors, stress concentration factors, and 1D worst-case vs. RSS statistical tolerance stack-up analysis. Digital Design Paradigms: Parametric feature modeling, generative topology optimization, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for real-time stress feedback, and Model-Based Definition (MBD) standards (ASME Y14.5 / STEP AP242). Applied Pedagogy: 4-column systems engineering trade-off matrix, seven cross-sector industrial failure case studies across aerospace, automotive, energy, and robotics, an interactive HTML5 canvas beam stress simulator, and six multi-step quantitative worked examples with explicit engineering interpretations. candidates.title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE DESIGN AND PARAMETRIC MODELING IN CAD FOR OPTIMIZATION OF AEROSPACE COMPONENT STRUCTURES
candidates.abstract: This paper discusses modern approaches to the design of load-bearing structures for aerospace equipment using topology optimization and generative design methods. The need to integrate parametric modeling to ensure the manufacturability of complex geometric shapes is sub-stantiated. It is shown that the application of additive technologies in combination with generative design allows reducing the weight of components by 40–50% while maintaining their strength characteristics.

candidates.title: Beyond overall accuracy: subgroup performance and threshold calibration of AI-assisted chest radiography for equity-oriented pulmonary tuberculosis screening
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted computer-aided detection (CAD) can expand access to chest radiography interpretation for pulmonary tuberculosis screening and triage, but high overall discrimination does not ensure safety at a deployed threshold. This focused narrative Mini Review synthesizes evidence on subgroup performance, threshold calibration, external validity, and implementation of CAD for adult pulmonary tuberculosis. Smear-negative, asymptomatic, and some HIV-associated disease may be less radiographically visible, increasing false-negative risk. Conversely, previous tuberculosis and competing chronic abnormalities reduce specificity and concentrate unnecessary confirmatory testing. Sex, age, geography, clinical setting, verification design, and software version can further alter operating performance. A numerical threshold is therefore not a portable algorithm property but a context-specific clinical resource-allocation policy. We propose a lifecycle in which programs define the intended use, lock the product and version, conduct representative local validation, select an operating point under explicit sensitivity and capacity constraints, audit clinically relevant subgroups, and monitor the complete care pathway. Stratified thresholds and multivariable models may improve selected settings, but current evidence does not justify replacing robust local calibration and governance. Prospective evaluations should compare threshold strategies under common verification standards and report missed cases, referral burden, treatment initiation, and patient-important outcomes.

candidates.title: Making What AI Cannot: Generative AI and Knowledge Through Making
candidates.abstract: Contemporary industrial designers have increasing access to Generative AI, computer-aided design (CAD), and fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printing. These tools can expand the possibilities available to individual designers, but their value cannot be understood only through the outputs they produce. This thesis examines how transferable knowledge can emerge through a practice-based design process that uses these tools, with particular emphasis on Generative AI. The research uses the design and fabrication of a free-standing loudspeaker as a vehicle for inquiry. Grounded in Research through Design and structured through Programmatic Design Research, the project was organised as a sequence of connected engagements involving visual and technical exploration, AI-assisted inquiry, CAD development, material experiments, comparative testing, practitioner feedback, fabrication, assembly, and reflection. Each engagement produced artefacts, observations, and takeaways that informed the direction of those that followed. The project demonstrates that transferable design knowledge was generated through the multiple interactions among these activities and shows how designer judgement emerged as a crucial part of the process, shaping how outputs were interpreted, which assumptions required proving, and which findings were rejected, revised, or carried forward. Generative AI supported exploration, technical questioning, comparison, and reflection, but its outputs were uneven and required further investigation through CAD, physical making, testing, and external feedback. CAD allowed possibilities to become controlled geometry while exposing material and assembly requirements. FDM printing brought these decisions into reality, revealing constraints involving tolerances, print behaviour, and material behaviour. The thesis argues that Programmatic Design Research provides a useful structure for turning these situated experiences into communicable and documented knowledge. By showing how ideas were generated, tested, rejected, revised, and carried between engagements, the research makes the design process open to reflection and extension by others. Its contribution is both the loudspeaker artefact and a transferable account of how contemporary tools, particularly Generative AI, can be investigated through contemporary industrial design practice.

candidates.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit, a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.

candidates.title: USE OF GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DESIGNING ROBOTIC MODELS USING ENGINEERING GRAPHICS
candidates.abstract: The article examines the possibilities of using generative artificial intelligence in teaching the discipline “Engineering and Computer Graphics” in the design of robotic models for the processing industry. The feasibility of integrating generative artificial intelligence models into the design process of robotic systems as a means of developing spatial thinking, graphic competence, design skills, and digital skills of agricultural university students is substantiated. It is established that modern generative systems (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Claude, DALL·E, etc.) support all stages of educational design, from developing technical specifications and generating product concepts to creating drawings and three-dimensional models, visualizing designs, preparing technical documentation, and analyzing possible design solutions. A methodology for using generative artificial intelligence in the educational project “Design of a Robotic Manipulator” is proposed. The methodology is based on the principles of project-based learning, STEM education, the competency-based approach, and the use of CAD systems. A structural model for integrating generative artificial intelligence into the process of graphic training has been developed. It includes the stages of problem formulation, concept generation, sketch creation, three-dimensional modeling, preparation of design documentation, and expert evaluation of the finished product. It is demonstrated that the use of generative AI contributes to increasing students’ motivation, developing engineering thinking, fostering digital literacy, and reducing the time required for routine operations in the design of robotic models.

candidates.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly
candidates.abstract: Creating digital garments from existing two-dimensional patterns remains a time-consuming process. Although patterns are widely available in digital form, their assembly in garment CAD software involves manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of the pattern panels for drape simulation. We present two learning-based approaches that automate both tasks using the 2D vector pattern as their sole input. Our automatic sewing model operates at the segment level, leveraging a Transformer encoder with multiple prediction heads. Our novel architecture supports many-to-many, ordered segment correspondences, as well as hems, overlapping seams needed for multilayer garments, and construction properties such as seam allowances and stitch types, required for the finished virtual garment but neglected by previous methods. A complementary panel-level model predicts body-region assignments, layers, and placement coordinates to initialize the drape simulation. We evaluate both models on a curated dataset of 4,035 professionally assembled garment instances. The sewing model exactly recovers all seam and hem topologies of 63.3\% of test garments, while the arrangement model meets the specified placement criteria for all panels in 66.2\% of test garments. We also integrate both methods into garment CAD software, demonstrating automatic assembly of successfully predicted garments.

candidates.title: Coarse-Graining Recursive Expert Computation: Continuation-Relative Interfaces and Failure Modes
candidates.abstract: Computational coarse-graining aims to replace a sequence of updates with a cheaper module while preserving task performance. We present a continuation-relative evaluation framework that assesses replacements through the computation that follows them, using downstream task quality and total execution cost as joint criteria. The framework distinguishes boundary representations, summaries of skipped computation, executed operations, and downstream loss. It makes interfaces and permitted deployment information explicit, combines fine-path references with directly trained controls using the same shortened architecture, and accounts for selection overhead. An exact loss decomposition separates replacement effects at a fixed downstream action from effects of changing that action. A finite construction shows how retained information can reduce the stipulated cost of zero-error prediction under fixed information and controller restrictions. Experiments in two frozen pretrained language models show that representation fidelity and task loss can favor different fitting objectives. In a prespecified comparison on a 1.7-billion-parameter model, next-token-loss training lowers in-distribution negative log-likelihood by 0.1901 nats per scored token compared with reconstructing the skipped blocks' output, using the same optimizer and update count. This ranking reverses in all nine paired comparisons under distribution shift. In a recursive expert prototype, the jointly adapted candidate lowers task error relative to frozen-bank and router-only baselines, but trails directly trained controls, and the tested input-only selectors fail the joint quality-cost criteria. Together, the protocol and studies provide explicit criteria and diagnostics for distinguishing useful computational replacement from local approximation gains within specified interfaces and evaluation settings.

candidates.title: Large language model-assisted CAD-RADS classification: structured report extraction, accuracy, and clinical decision-making risk of ChatGPT-4o/5 and DeepSeek-R1
candidates.abstract: Objective To compare ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 in assigning main Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from findings-only coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) reports and to characterize management-relevant classification errors. Methods This retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study included 2,100 category-balanced findings-only CCTA reports (300 per CAD-RADS category). Two experienced CCTA radiologists graded the English-translated reports; 12 disagreements were resolved by a third. ChatGPT-4o was evaluated in standard mode, ChatGPT-5 in Thinking mode, and DeepSeek-R1 in Deep Thinking mode; model generation and inference mode therefore varied together. Exact-match accuracy with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs), paired comparisons, and unweighted Gwet AC1 with 95% CIs were calculated. Management-relevant transitions and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) findings among high-risk downgrades were analyzed. Results DeepSeek-R1 had an exact-match accuracy of 82.57% (95% CI, 80.89–84.13) and AC1 of 0.797 (95% CI, 0.778–0.816). ChatGPT-5 had an accuracy of 80.19% (95% CI, 78.43–81.84) and AC1 of 0.769 (95% CI, 0.749–0.789), whereas ChatGPT-4o had an accuracy of 53.62% (95% CI, 51.48–55.74) and AC1 of 0.460 (95% CI, 0.435–0.485). Cochran's Q test was significant (Q = 657.87; df = 2; P < 0.001); after Holm correction, DeepSeek-R1 also outperformed ChatGPT-5 in the paired comparison ( P = 0.026), and both outperformed ChatGPT-4o (both P < 0.001). ChatGPT-4o downgraded 127/900 (14.11%) reference high-risk reports to CAD-RADS 3 or lower. Of these 127 cases, 65 underwent DSA within three months; DSA supported the original high-risk assessment in 56/65 (86.15%). The corresponding high-risk downgrade proportions were 37/900 (4.11%) for ChatGPT-5 and 23/900 (2.56%) for DeepSeek-R1. Conclusion The DeepSeek-R1 Deep Thinking and ChatGPT-5 Thinking configurations achieved higher accuracy than ChatGPT-4o in standard mode. Because model generation and inference mode varied together, the results do not isolate a model-family effect. LLMs merit further evaluation for secondary structuring when no documented CAD-RADS category is available, but should not overwrite a radiologist-assigned category or independently determine management.

candidates.title: CAD/CAM Technologies, Three-Dimensional Printing, and Contemporary Dental Materials
candidates.abstract: CAD/CAM technologies have transformed the production of fixed prosthodontic restorations from a craft based on manual skill into a standardized and measurable digital process. This chapter addresses, for dental students in their clinical years and for early-career clinicians, the fundamental principles of CAD/CAM systems, digital and artificial intelligence-assisted restoration design, milling and three-dimensional printing technologies, contemporary restorative materials, the factors influencing material selection, accuracy and quality control in digital manufacturing, and the biocompatible and smart materials of the future, in the light of the current and verified literature. The digital workflow comprises three interdependent links—data acquisition, design, and manufacturing—and the quality of the final restoration is limited by the weakest link in the chain. Although milling remains the gold standard for definitive restorations, additive manufacturing has become established for interim restorations, models, and surgical guides, and it is a rapidly maturing alternative for definitive restorations. On the material side, the rise of monolithic zirconia, the diversification of lithium silicate glass-ceramics, and the establishment of resin-matrix ceramics in minimally invasive applications offer the clinician a broad range of options with varying levels of evidence. Current systematic-review and meta-analytic evidence shows that AI-assisted design shortens design time and improves reproducibility, but that human oversight remains indispensable. Clinical success depends on manufacturing the right material with validated parameters for the right indication and applying it with an appropriate adhesive or conventional cementation protocol. Accuracy should be defined by its trueness and precision components, marginal fit should be evaluated against clinical acceptability thresholds, and quality control should be maintained at every link of the digital chain. The graded, bioactive, self-healing, and stimuli-responsive materials of the future, together with additively manufactured ceramics, signal a transition from passive to smart materials in restorative dentistry.

candidates.title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
candidates.abstract: Practical ship design requires localized refinement and performance evaluation. This paper presents a reward-directed diffusion framework for localized hull optimization. Parametric masking during dataset generation restricts geometric changes to selected variables, including the bulbous bow and forebody, while preserving full-hull continuity. Surrogate-assisted sequential Monte Carlo sampling targets reduced predicted calm-water resistance, with stability retained through training data and displacement matched during screening. An automated viscous free-surface CFD pipeline, validated against measurements for two benchmark container ships, evaluates a generated variant and GenHull E, a hull refined by a naval architect within the same representation. At matched KRISO Container Ship (KCS) displacement, the generated variant has comparable total resistance at $F_n=0.195$ but 45-50% higher resistance at $F_n=0.250$ and $0.260$, missed by empirical screening. GenHull E achieves 6-8% lower total resistance up to $F_n=0.240$ but higher resistance above $F_n=0.250$ as opposing friction and pressure trends reverse the gains. Aggregating resistance across this crossover can conceal tradeoffs that emerge when friction and pressure components are evaluated separately. The assessment reveals an inability to represent a faired bulbous bow and a reward lacking viscous pressure and stability terms. These findings show how high-fidelity assessment informs improved representations and objectives for physically realizable generative designs.

candidates.title: Look Where You Can: Active View Selection for CAD Reconstruction under Occlusion
candidates.abstract: CAD reconstruction methods assume a luxury reality rarely grants: unrestricted visual access to the object, photographed from any desired angle. Real objects, however, are scene-embedded, bolted against walls, wedged into corners, resting on floors, where the scene renders much of the view sphere unreachable and the remaining views unequally informative. We introduce \textbf{SightCAD}, a framework for parametric CAD reconstruction that treats view feasibility as a first-class constraint. In this work we consider objects from standard CAD benchmarks embedded in realistic indoor scenes with physically derived visibility constraints over a discrete view sphere. A learned view selector must choose $K$ feasible views for a vision--language model (VLM) that generates executable CadQuery code, scored by geometric fidelity of the executed solid. Because reward arrives only after discrete view selection, autoregressive generation, and CAD-kernel execution, we propose a joint training paradigm in which the view selector and the CAD-generation VLM are trained together against this reward. The learned selection policy departs sharply from random, uniform, and coverage-greedy alternatives, outperforming surface-area maximization (SA-max) by up to $6.4$ Intersection-over-Union (IoU) points across budgets $K\in\{1,\dots,5\}$. The full system surpasses strong external baselines on scene-embedded, occluded multi-view renders of DeepCAD and Fusion360 objects ($+21$ and $+17$ effective-mIoU points over the best baseline, respectively), as well as on test-time domain-canonicalized real images from the industrial T-LESS benchmark and on both synthetic and real images from the MP6D industrial metal-parts benchmark, while producing the highest rate of executable programs of any method compared (invalid-code rate ${\leq}1.5\%$).

candidates.title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
candidates.abstract: False negatives remain a critical limitation of computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems for breast cancer screening due to delayed detection and treatment. To address this issue, we propose a counterfactual data augmentation strategy that generates healthy mammograms by "erasing" lesions from anomalous images, thereby enriching the training distribution. We train a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model on BI-RADS 1 (healthy) mammograms and use a RePaint-based sampling strategy to inpaint realistic normal tissue within annotated lesion bounding boxes. The resulting healthy counterfactuals replace annotated lesion regions with realistic healthy tissue while preserving patient-specific anatomical structure, as supported by similarity metrics between real and generated images. Image realism was further assessed by radiologists and found to be consistent with the original dataset quality. We evaluate counterfactual augmentation across four representative classifier architectures: a convolutional neural network (ConvNeXt), a vision transformer (ViT), a vision-language model pre-trained on mammogram-report pairs (Mammo-CLIP) and a multi-scale attention-based multiple-instance learning framework (FPN-MIL). Experiments conducted on the VinDr-Mammo dataset show improvements in sensitivity across all architectures, particularly at 80\% fixed specificity, contributing towards more reliable CAD systems for breast cancer. Code is available at: https://github.com/ines03garcia/diffusion-based-counterfactual-generation.

candidates.title: Automated Assembly Instruction Generation from CAD Models Using Grounded Large Language Models: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework
candidates.abstract: Assembly documentation is a downstream manufacturing artifact that is still usually authored by interpreting CAD models by hand. Structured product data and large language models are both available, yet studies of CAD interpretation, assembly sequence planning, instruction writing, and human oversight have largely proceeded separately. This paper formulates CAD-grounded assembly instruction generation: the production of natural-language assembly procedures constrained by structured engineering information extracted from CAD models. The proposed framework maps a STEP assembly to a typed ProductGraph intermediate representation, derives a precedence order by deterministic topological sorting, realizes each step as language conditioned only on selected graph context, attaches per-step visual documentation, and applies rule-based and model-assisted checks. PDF export remains disabled until a human reviewer resolves every quality flag. The case study establishes endto-end feasibility on a built-in six-part reference assembly: the pipeline preserves a reported assembly order and carries quantity, material, and torque into an exported manual page. Generalization and geometric validation remain open empirical questions. The contribution is an architecture that separates engineering state, deterministic reasoning, grounded language realization, verification, and human release.

candidates.title: Integrating Sustainability and Life Cycle Assessment into CAD-Driven Product Design: A Systematic Review of Frameworks, Additive Manufacturing Trade-offs and Industry 4.0 Enablers
candidates.abstract: With decarbonisation goals and new ecodesign regulations, life cycle assessment (LCA) is increasingly becoming a function of computer-aided design (CAD). This paper undertakes a systematic review following PRISMA 2020 statement of research related to integrating sustainability and LCA into CAD driven product design. Peer-reviewed journal articles and conference papers published from 2016 to 2026 were retrieved from the databases Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and ScienceDirect (Google Scholar was used as a supporting database) and synthesized in a thematic synthesis. The evidence is presented in six streams: CAD–LCA integration frameworks; sustainable and generative optimisation; design for additive manufacturing (DfAM) and topology optimisation; process-parameter optimisation as a source for life cycle inventory (LCI) data; Industry 4.0 and digital twin (DT) based assessment; and social and organisational enablers of adoption. The review concludes that most of the life cycle impact occurs at the conceptual stage, and that tools for environmental assessment at the conceptual level are not sufficiently mature at the detailed design stage, when geometry and material are fixed. There is a constant dilemma between the material savings possible with topology optimisation and AM, and the extra energy needed to produce structures using these routes does not necessarily mean they have a smaller footprint. Experimental process-optimisation studies demonstrate that the choice of process parameters has a significant effect on the energy used, scrap produced and the consumption of tools, in the cases of machining, moulding, finishing and material-extrusion printing, but the results from these studies are generally not transferred to inventories to use in design tools. A closed-loop system which integrates design, assessment, process and operation data is suggested to inform future work, which can be layered.

candidates.title: Role of Computed Tomography in the evaluation of coronary artery disease: A prospective study
candidates.abstract: Background of the StudyCoronary artery disease (CAD) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide and poses a significant healthcare burden in developing countries such as India.The increasing prevalence of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, obesity, smoking, dyslipidemia, and sedentary lifestyle has contributed to the rising incidence of CAD (Virani et al., 2020;Gupta et al., 2016).Conventional invasive coronary angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing coronary artery stenosis; however, it is invasive and associated with procedural risks.Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography (CTCA) has emerged as an effective non-invasive imaging modality for evaluating coronary artery anatomy, plaque characterization, coronary calcium scoring, and luminal stenosis.Recent developments in multidetector computed tomography (MDCT), Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS), fractional flow reserve CT (FFRCT), and artificial intelligence-assisted imaging have further enhanced diagnostic accuracy and prognostic assessment in CAD patients (Cury et al., 2016; Dey et al., 2019). Aim and ObjectivesThe present study aimed to evaluate the role of Computed Tomography in the diagnosis and assessment of coronary artery disease among patients with suspected CAD. ObjectivesThe assess the diagnostic utility of CT coronary angiography in detecting coronary artery stenosis.To evaluate plaque morphology and coronary artery calcium scoring in CAD patients.To classify coronary artery disease using the CAD-RADS reporting system.To determine the relationship between CT findings and severity of coronary artery disease.To assess the effectiveness of CT as a non-invasive imaging modality in CAD evaluation.Methodology A prospective observational study was conducted among patients clinically suspected of coronary artery disease and referred for CT coronary angiography in the Department of Radiodiagnosis at a tertiary care hospital.All patients underwent multidetector CT coronary angiography using standardized acquisition protocols after obtaining informed consent.Demographic data, cardiovascular risk factors, coronary artery calcium scores, plaque characteristics, and severity of luminal stenosis were recorded.CAD-RADS classification was used for standardized interpretation and reporting.Statistical analysis was performed to determine the diagnostic performance and clinical significance of CT findings in CAD evaluation. ResultsThe study demonstrated that CT coronary angiography effectively identified coronary artery stenosis, calcified and noncalcified plaques, and coronary calcium burden in patients with suspected CAD.Significant associations were observed between cardiovascular risk factors and severity of coronary artery disease.CAD-RADS classification provided a standardized and clinically valuable approach for disease stratification and management planning.CT imaging showed high sensitivity and diagnostic accuracy for detecting significant coronary artery lesions and identifying high-risk plaque characteristics associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes (Budoff et al., 2008;Hoffmann et al., 2012).Discussion Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography has become an important non-invasive diagnostic modality due to its high spatial resolution, rapid image acquisition, and ability to assess both coronary lumen and vessel wall pathology.The findings of the present study are consistent with previous studies reporting high diagnostic accuracy of CTCA in CAD assessment.Advanced CT applications such as coronary calcium scoring, plaque characterization, FFRCT, and AI-based quantitative plaque analysis contribute significantly to early diagnosis, cardiovascular risk stratification, and treatment planning (Dey et al., 2019; Knuuti et al., 2020).Although radiation exposure and contrast-related complications remain "Role of Computed Tomography in the evaluation of coronary artery disease: A prospective study" IJDDT, Volume16 Issue 55s,2026Page: 501 concerns, recent dose-reduction protocols and technological advancements have significantly improved patient safety and expanded the clinical utility of CT imaging (Gulati et al., 2021). ConclusionComputed Tomography Coronary Angiography is a highly effective, safe, and non-invasive imaging modality for the evaluation of coronary artery disease.It provides accurate assessment of coronary stenosis, plaque characterization, coronary calcium burden, and cardiovascular risk stratification.CTCA plays a significant role in the early diagnosis and management of CAD patients and may reduce the need for unnecessary invasive coronary angiography in selected cases. SummaryThe study highlights the growing importance of Computed Tomography in the diagnosis and management of coronary artery disease.CT coronary angiography demonstrated excellent capability in detecting coronary artery abnormalities, assessing plaque burden, and guiding patient management through standardized CAD-RADS reporting.Integration of advanced imaging technologies further enhances the role of CT in cardiovascular medicine.Recommendations 1. CT coronary angiography should be considered as a first-line non-invasive imaging modality in selected patients with suspected CAD. 2. CAD-RADS reporting should be routinely implemented for standardized interpretation and communication.3. Large-scale multicenter studies should be conducted to evaluate long-term prognostic outcomes.4. Advanced technologies such as FFRCT and artificial intelligence-assisted imaging should be integrated into routine clinical practice.5. Radiation dose optimization protocols should be followed to improve patient safety.

candidates.title: Retinal and coronary imaging in type 1 diabetes: links between retinopathy and subclinical cardiovascular disease
candidates.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of premature morbidity and mortality in individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), despite advances in glycemic management and cardiovascular prevention. Conventional cardiovascular risk assessment may underestimate risk in T1DM, particularly among younger asymptomatic individuals, highlighting the need for markers of early vascular injury. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a microvascular complication of T1DM, is increasingly recognized as a marker of systemic vascular dysfunction rather than an isolated ocular disorder. Non-invasive retinal visualization may provide insight into vascular and atherosclerotic disease. This mini-review summarizes evidence linking DR with subclinical coronary artery disease (CAD) and cardiovascular outcomes in T1DM, focusing on coronary artery calcium (CAC) and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). Observational and longitudinal studies consistently link DR severity with CAC burden, coronary plaque burden, silent CAD, and cardiovascular outcomes, independent of traditional risk factors. Albuminuria and diabetic kidney disease may provide complementary evidence of a broader microvascular phenotype associated with cardiovascular risk. Advances in retinal imaging, including optical coherence tomography angiography and artificial intelligence-based oculomics, support the role of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular risk prediction. CAC scoring remains valuable for detecting subclinical coronary atherosclerosis, while CCTA characterizes calcified and non-calcified plaque. Emerging evidence suggests that integrating retinal and microvascular markers with coronary imaging may improve identification of asymptomatic individuals at increased cardiovascular risk and support intervention. Although data are observational and prospective validation is required, multimodal strategies combining clinical risk factors, retinal biomarkers, albuminuria, CAC, and CCTA may enhance cardiovascular risk stratification in T1DM.

candidates.title: End-to-End Autonomous Generation of Human Assembly Plans
candidates.abstract: Turning a CAD design into an assembly plan is still largely done by hand, requiring engineers to reason about geometric feasibility, tool access, stability, and the ergonomics of human assembly. In this work, we encode long-established design for assembly (DfA) principles into a contained, end-to-end approach for generating assembly plans. Our approach takes only a mesh assembly and produces either a step-by-step assembly manual or a structured failure report, requiring no joint metadata, fastener annotations, or additional information. Four major components of a manufacturing plan are addressed autonomously: an assembly tool list, the assembly sequence and subassemblies, an assembly manual, and design feedback for improving assemblability. For determining the sequence plan, we systematically disassemble the object in a physics simulator and apply a cost function that encodes DfA principles. Manual generation, tool labelling, and assembly feedback rely primarily on multimodal large language models. Compared with a baseline that always removes the outermost part first from Tian et al., DfA-aware sequence planning reduces simulated assembly time, measured with a robot-arm assembly-time proxy, by 35% on 136 assemblies of 5 to 30 parts. The correct tool is selected for 88.6% of assembly steps. A vision-language model judge compares the generated manuals against ablated variants, identifying which page elements carry the information a reader needs. The presented approach and open-source code are available for use by engineers or AI agents looking to rapidly accelerate the creation of manufacturing plans for a given product design.

candidates.title: Confidence-based classification of clinically significant prostate cancer on biparametric MRI using Monte Carlo dropout and Grad-CAM visualization
candidates.abstract: Objective: Accurate early diagnosis of Clinically Significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is crucial for improving patient survival rates. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable, confidence-based deep learning model for csPCa classification using biparametric MRI (bpMRI). Methods: A retrospective analysis was conducted on bpMRI data from 410 patients. A classification model was constructed using the visual geometry group 16-layer (VGG-16) network, incorporating gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) for uncertainty estimation, and a rejection mechanism. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC). Results: Across all predictions, the confidence-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.3% before rejection. At a confidence threshold of 0.8, 80.8% of predictions were retained, among which the selective accuracy was 94.6%, with 99 false-positive and 2 false-negative predictions. Besides, the model's accuracy outperformed that of a senior radiologist (94.6% vs 90.8%). Qualitative Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that the classifier frequently assigned high activation to MRI regions considered suspicious for csPCa; however, quantitative spatial agreement with lesion annotations was not assessed. Conclusion: This confidence-based model identifies csPCa lesions and provides reliable confidence scores without pixel-level annotations. By rejecting uncertain predictions, it enhances the transparency and safety of clinical decision-making.

candidates.title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use
candidates.abstract: Reconstructing an editable CAD model from a 3D shape remains a challenging engineering task. Existing methods can propose CAD operations, but no single source of proposals works equally well across different part geometries and stages of reconstruction. We introduce CADFather, an autonomous agentic system that coordinates complementary tools to recover parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes. A vision-language assistant inspects renders of the target and intermediate reconstructions, then decides which candidate CAD programs to extend, which tools to invoke, how many proposals to generate, and when to finish. Learned and algorithmic tools propose CAD operations, while numerical optimization refines the parameters of existing programs. Proposed or refined programs are executed and evaluated to provide feedback for subsequent decisions. The agent maintains alternative candidate programs for each target part and preserves the best valid result throughout reconstruction. CADFather uses pretrained generation and assistant models without additional training. We evaluate reconstruction quality and execution validity on the full DeepCAD, Fusion360, and MCB test sets, as well as on CADENA-Bench, CADBench, and BenchCAD. We additionally analyze computational cost and the trade-off between cost and reconstruction quality.

candidates.title: PrimitiveCAD: An LLM-Based Point-to-CAD Reconstruction with Primitive-Aware Tokenization and Operation Alignment
candidates.abstract: Large-model-based point-to-CAD generation holds immense potential for advancing industrial design and enhancing 3D modeling efficiency. However, most existing methods approach the problem as a general point-cloud encoding and token prediction task, neglecting the tokenization and supervision specifically for CAD-related primitives. As a result, these methods often struggle to accurately reconstruct the intricate primitive structures. To address this limitation, we propose PrimitiveCAD, a novel multi-stage paradigm for point-to-CAD reconstruction that enhances the geometric accuracy of generated CAD models while better preserving critical geometric features. First, we introduce a primitive-aware point cloud tokenization model, enabling the system to learn more robust geometric representations from CAD point clouds. Next, we perform supervised finetuning on a large language model (LLM) and introduce an operation alignment loss to align key CAD operation frequencies, thereby improving the preservation of global shape features. Finally, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) and introduce a feature-line alignment reward to further reduce stochasticity and enhance the fine-grained preservation of geometric features. Experiments on the DeepCAD and Fusion360 datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in code validity, geometric accuracy, and geometric feature preservation.
